title: The question and its field-theoretic answer
content: The header frames the open question — what exactly is the field of origami-constructible numbers — and states the answer proved here: it is the smallest subfield of ℂ closed under both square roots and cube roots. Origami (Huzita–Justin single-fold) does everything straightedge-and-compass does plus one new operation, real cube-root extraction, because a single fold can produce a common tangent to two parabolas. The five deliverables (structure, closure, minimality, cubic-solving, witnesses) are laid out, and the connection to the arithmetic '2^a·3^b' degree criterion of the sibling entries is recorded.
mathContext: Origami numbers $=$ closure of $\mathbb{Q}$ inside $\mathbb{C}$ under $+,-,\times,\div,\sqrt{\cdot},\sqrt[3]{\cdot}$.

title: IsOrigami: the inductive closure
content: The heart of the formalization is to model the origami numbers not analytically but as a generation principle: IsOrigami is the least predicate on ℂ containing every rational and closed under addition, negation, multiplication, inversion, and — the two extraction constructors — any w with w²=a or w³=a of an origami a. Encoding the field as an inductive type is what makes both the minimality theorem (one case per constructor) and Cardano's formula (the √ and ∛ steps are literally the sqrt/cbrt constructors) fall out by structural induction.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsOrigami}$ is the least predicate with $\mathbb{Q}\subseteq$ it, closed under $+,-,\times,{}^{-1}$ and under $w^2=a,\,w^3=a$.

title: Derived operations: 0, 1, subtraction, division
content: Subtraction and division are not separate constructors but derived: a − b = a + (−b) and a / b = a · b⁻¹, with 0 and 1 coming from rat 0 and rat 1. Keeping the inductive type minimal (only the truly primitive operations) shortens every structural induction later, since there are fewer cases to discharge.

title: origamiField: packaging the closure as a Subfield ℂ
content: The predicate IsOrigami is bundled into a genuine Subfield ℂ, discharging each field-axiom membership obligation with the corresponding inductive constructor. Membership is definitionally IsOrigami (mem_origamiField is Iff.rfl), so the bundled object and the raw predicate are interchangeable in proofs.

title: Closure under roots and conjugation
content: Closure under square and cube roots is immediate (the sqrt/cbrt constructors). Closure under complex conjugation is the first real induction: conjugation commutes with all four field operations and sends an n-th root of a to an n-th root of conj(a), so each constructor case reproduces itself after conjugating. This conjugation-closedness matches Alperin's characterization, which lists conjugation alongside √ and ∛.
mathContext: $a\in F,\,w^2=a\Rightarrow w\in F$; likewise for $w^3$; and $z\in F\Rightarrow\bar z\in F$.

title: The exact characterization: origamiField is least
content: This is the headline theorem. origamiField_le_of_closed proves that ANY subfield K ⊆ ℂ closed under square and cube roots contains every origami number, by structural induction on IsOrigami: rationals are in K (it's a subfield), the field-operation cases are K's own closure, and the two root cases are exactly the closure hypotheses on K. Combined with origamiField's own closure, origamiField_isLeast packages this as IsLeast — origamiField is the least element of the set of root-closed subfields. This is precisely the field-theoretic object the open question asked to identify.

title: Origami solves quadratics: completing the square
content: Every root of an origami-coefficient quadratic r²+br+c=0 is origami. The proof completes the square: 2r+b squares to the discriminant b²−4c (an origami number), so 2r+b is an origami square root, and r = ((2r+b)−b)/2 is recovered by origami field operations. This is the part of origami's power already shared with straightedge-and-compass (only square roots needed).

title: Cardano's formula inside the origami field
content: The operational core: every depressed cubic r³+pr+q with origami coefficients has an origami root, by a full formalization of Cardano's formula. A square root s of the discriminant (q/2)²+(p/3)³ and a cube root u of −q/2+s are both origami (the √ and ∛ closures), and r = u − p/(3u) is the Cardano root. A separate p=0 branch handles the degenerate u=0 case (then r³=−q is a direct cube root). The resolvent identity v³=−q/2−s and the cubic vanishing are closed by linear_combination/ring. This is exactly where the cube-root constructor — origami's new power — does work straightedge-and-compass cannot.

title: Every root of an origami cubic is origami
content: Upgrades 'has an origami root' to 'every root is origami'. Given any root r and the Cardano root r₀, the cubic factors as (r−r₀)(r²+r₀r+(r₀²+p))=0. Either r=r₀, or r is a root of the residual quadratic with origami coefficients (r₀²+p), handled by origamiField_root_quadratic. This closes the gap between existence and the full membership statement needed for the witnesses.
mathContext: $r^3+pr+q = (r-r_0)(r^2+r_0 r + (r_0^2+p))$; the quadratic factor has origami coefficients.

title: Witnesses: i, ∛2 (Delian), and cos 20° (trisection)
content: Three concrete origami numbers make the abstract characterization tangible. i is a square root of −1. A cube root of 2 settles the Delian problem of doubling the cube — impossible with straightedge-and-compass, achievable with origami. cos 20° is origami because the triple-angle identity 4cos³θ−3cosθ=cos3θ at θ=π/9 makes it a root of 8x³−6x−1=0 (here written x³−(3/4)x−1/8), an origami-coefficient cubic, so origamiField_root_cubic applies. This is the formal statement that origami trisects the 60° angle — the classical impossibility dissolved by the extra cube-root power.
